title: Patch triage rotation and SIEM export playbook (Sep 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for handling vulnerability scanner outputs across the organization, automating evidence collection for audits, and mapping vulnerability lifecycle events into our SIEM/export schema. The goal is to reduce mean time to remediation (MTTR), provide deterministic audit artifacts, and ensure patch SLAs are enforced in a scalable on-call rotation model.

Scope: 
- Applies to all internal and customer-facing services in our cloud fleet and Dedicated nodes.
- Includes dependency scanning (SCA), image/container scanning, OS-level scanner outputs (Qualys/Tenable/Trivy), and dependency-license notes.
- Excludes air-gapped Private deployments until specific customer agreements are in place (see Private deployment checklist below).

Status & intent: Draft -> moving to in_review after 2026-11-10. This doc intentionally contains chatty notes, TODOs, and sample scripts so the SRE/Platform teams can iterate quickly.

High-level flow (what happens when a scan fires):
1) Scanner ingestion: scheduled scanner runs land JSON/CSV outputs in the vuln-bucket (s3://redwood-scanner-outputs) and are forwarded to the vuln-ingest lambda.
2) Normalization: vuln-ingest normalizes into our canonical schema (fields listed below) and writes a canonical record to the vuln-events topic (kafka).
3) Triage automation: triage-bot enriches records with owner hints (from CODEOWNERS, infra tags), first-seen timestamp, and dependency-resolution links. If severity >= critical or exploitability == true, triage-bot opens a JIRA ticket SEC-xxx and triggers a P1 PagerDuty alert per rotation rules.
4) Patch plan & evidence: remediation owner attaches evidence (build logs, CVE patch commits, image digest after rebuild) to the JIRA ticket using the evidence-collector tool. Evidence metadata is mirrored to the audit-log service.
5) SIEM export: once evidence metadata is present and ticket status moves to remediation_in_progress, the SIEM export connector emits a normalized event and fields specified in the SIEM mapping below.

Canonical vulnerability record (fields we guarantee):
- vuln_id: string (scanner id or composite key)
- cve: string (CVE-YYYY-NNNN) or vendor advisory id
- title: short title from scanner
- description: first 512 chars
- severity: critical/high/medium/low/none (normalized)
- cvss_v3: string score or "n/a"
- product: service name / image name / library path
- component: file/path or package name
- fixed_in: version string or "none"
- first_seen: ISO8601
- last_seen: ISO8601
- exploitability: true|false
- scanner_vendor: e.g., trivy/tenable/qualys/oss-sca
- scanner_raw_url: s3 path to original output
- owners: list (primary, secondary) as csv string
- jira_ticket: issue key or "none"
- evidence_ids: csv of evidence blob ids
- remediation_eta: ISO8601 or "scheduled"
- remediation_status: new/triaged/remediation_in_progress/remediated/verified/wont_fix

Severity mapping heuristics (early notes):
- Critical: CVSS >= 9.0 OR exploitability==true OR canonical product == control_plane (k8s api, deployment pipeline)
- High: 7.0 <= CVSS < 9.0 OR package has active exploit in public repos within 30d
- Medium: 4.0 <= CVSS < 7.0
- Low: CVSS < 4.0
- Note: scanner vendors have different default severities; rely on normalized cvss_v3 when present.

Patch SLAs (proposal):
- Critical: 48 hours to remediation plan, 7 days to remediation (target 72 hours for infra-control-plane)
- High: 7 days to remediation plan, 30 days to remediation
- Medium: 30 days to remediation plan, 90 days to remediation
- Low: 90 days to remediation plan, 180 days to remediation
- Exceptions: documented via Jira workflow step "compensating_controls" and requires SOC/Eng lead approval.

On-call rotation / triage roles (operational draft):
- Primary on-call: first responder, create ticket, assign owner, kick off patch plan. Rotation: security rotation (weekly).
- Platform backup: if primary >= 4 hours unresolved, escalate to platform on-call.
- SRE verification: after remediation, SRE verifies patch on staging and production using smoke tests and rebuild hashes.
- CS/Customer notifications: if customer artifact affected (Dedicated/private), trigger CS runbook.

Evidence automation (collector notes + minimal recipe):
- Evidence types we collect: build artifacts (image digest), GitHub PR with fixing commit, CI logs showing tests passed, package upgrade diff, container scan post-rebuild results.
- Evidence upload flow: evidence-collector CLI uploads artifacts to evidence-bucket with metadata JSON (schema: evidence_id, vuln_id, uploader, timestamp, artifact_type, s3_path, sha256, notes).
- Sample CLI (pseudo):
  evidence-collector upload --vuln SEC-xxxx --artifact path/to/image-manifest.json --type image-manifest --notes "rebuild after bump to openssl 3.1.1"
- Automation hooks: when a PR that references the Jira ticket merges, a GitHub Action triggers the collector with the merged commit hash and image digest.

Audit log mapping (for compliance evidence):
- When evidence-collector writes metadata, we generate an audit_log entry with: event_type=vuln_evidence_uploaded, actor=CI/GitHubAction/username, resource=service_name, ref_id=evidence_id, timestamp, change_details (json string).
- RBAC implication: only security-admin or owner OR a service principal with role "vuln:evidence_uploader" can mark "verified" in Jira. This is enforced via RBAC v2 policy that maps service principals to actions.

SIEM export schema (fields exported per vuln event):
- event_id (UUID), event_time, vuln_id, cve, severity, cvss_v3, scanner_vendor, product, component, owner_team, jira_ticket, remediation_status, evidence_count, exploitability, first_seen, last_seen, remediation_eta, tags
- Enrichment fields: cloud_region, instance_id (if affected), image_digest, git_repo, commit_hash, risk_score (derived), sla_breach_expected (boolean)
- Export cadence: immediate for severity>=high, hourly aggregate for medium/low. Exports are sent to Splunk HTTP Event Collector and to our SIEM backup queue in S3.

Sample SIEM event (single-line example for devs):
{event_time: 2026-10-05T13:12:04Z, vuln_id: trivy-20261005-234, cve: CVE-2026-1234, severity: high, product: api-gateway, owner_team: platform-api, jira_ticket: SEC-3412, remediation_status: remediation_in_progress} 

Remediation tracking notes (what to attach to tickets):
- Patch PR link(s) and CI build ID(s)
- Post-patch scan results (before/after) with s3 paths
- Smoke test run ids and logs
- Rollout plan (canary %, timeline)
- Rollback plan and responsible owners
- If "wont_fix" document why and compensating controls (WAF rules, network ACLs)

Dependency review guidance (SCA):
- For npm/pip/maven: prefer explicit resolution to a fixed version; avoid transitive-only fixes without owner approval.
- If a fix introduces breaking API changes, document risk and timeline in the ticket and schedule a versioned rollout.
- Keep a dependency-owners table in CODEOWNERS-like file for libs that span multiple services. Triage-bot uses that to suggest owners.

Operational playbook for a P0/P1 after triage: quick checklist
- Confirm exploitability (search for exploit PoC public repos)
- Determine blast radius (which clusters/services/tenants)
- Apply temporary mitigations (network-level access control, WAF, rate-limit) and document in ticket
- Create patch PR and link evidence
- Schedule canary rollout and smoke test windows
- After successful canary, promote to full rollout and mark evidence
- Verify via post-rollout scans and close ticket when verified

Practical notes + scripts to keep in ops-scripts:
- Normalize scanner JSON: scripts/normalize_trivy.py -> outputs canonical JSON with fields above
- Evidence uploader: ops-scripts/evidence_uploader.py (lambda + CLI)
- SIEM exporter: ops-scripts/siem_forwarder.py (supports Splunk HEC and S3)
- Quick grep for open criticals: cat latest.json | jq -r '.[] | select(.severity=="Critical") | .vuln_id + " " + .product'

Known gaps TODOs (open items):
- [ ] Formalize RBAC v2 policy snippets and attach to this doc (SEC-PRIV-1001).
- [ ] Add Private-deployments evidence pathway (air-gapped uploads).
- [ ] Finalize SLA approval with Eng leadership and Legal for customer-impacting patches.
- [ ] Add automated unit for risk_score calculation (ML-based) into enrichment pipeline.
- [ ] Expose a lightweight dashboard in Redwood Console for active SLA breaches.

Appendix: Notes from triage rotation retrospective (2026-10-31)
- Rotation hit: too much manual evidence collection slowed verification. Automation via GitHub Actions + collector reduced verification time by ~40% in the pilot.
- Pager fatigue: refine alert thresholds for non-exploitable high severity unless blast radius > single dev cluster.
- Many SCA findings are false positives for downstream forks; add exact-path heuristics to triage-bot.
